page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core. It includes 2880 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core tests scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth tests fall into the bottom 25%. This memory constraint is reflected in weak performance for database operations and software compilation. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 offers a high density of local storage relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a resource-dense option for storage-heavy workloads without the premium cost of larger compute instances. However, the tradeoff is limited memory bandwidth and weak multi-threaded decompression performance. This profile makes the instance well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, redis caching, and light text processing. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive database operations, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference.

It features a substantial 2880 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, placing in the top 25% for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Conversely, memory read bandwidth is weak, scoring in the bottom 25% for both cached and uncached read operations. This resource profile offers high storage density relative to compute, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-centric tasks. The L4aos_v4 is best suited for static web serving, redis caching, and text processing, while it is less effective for memory-bound database operations or intensive multi-threaded compilation.
